A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCR-head study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original head-score analyses, CoT experiments, head-masking and attention-redistribution results, and character-level activation analyses, including appendix heatmaps.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds a layer-distribution analysis of OCR and retrieval heads in Section 6.2 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The evidence-patch construction, OCR scoring and head-selection procedure, and sink-token redistribution mechanism remain unchanged. The new distribution analysis examines the existing method's outputs.

E1.justification: Both versions use text/image passkey and NIAH tasks, single-character probes, OCR-VQA, DocVQA, MP-DocVQA, Natural Questions, and HotpotQA. The layer-distribution analysis adds no dataset, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: The unmodified-model baselines, retrieval-head comparisons, and random-head masking controls remain the same in the corresponding experiments. The new heatmap uses the existing OCR-versus-retrieval-head comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,200 sampled identification instances, 2–12 input images, the same thresholds, downstream F1 evaluation, and masking of 5, 10, or 20 heads. Section 6.2 analyzes existing scores without introducing a changed evaluation setting.

E4.justification: New Section 6.2 and Figure 7 examine whether OCR heads cluster in particular layers across the three existing models. The earlier CoT, masking, redistribution, and character-shape analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same reporting of random-head masking as mean plus/minus variance across five selections. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports layer-specific head distributions and counts: Qwen2-VL-2B has 11 OCR heads in layer 17 and 8 in layer 22; Qwen2-VL-7B has 10 in layer 14 and 11 in layer 22. Tables 1–4 and the existing character-level results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The retrieval-score, OCR-score, Jaccard-similarity, and attention-redistribution formulas in Equations 1–4 remain unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions. The revised conclusion adds the categorical claim that OCR-head masking leaves text-based QA 'unaffected,' strengthening v1's more general specialization claim and comparative discussion.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly interprets OCR heads as more focused and robust at attending to relevant text regions. Section 6.2 adds the interpretation of concentration in middle-to-late layers. The stated model-diversity and computational limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The documented preprocessing, head-selection settings, redistribution hyperparameter and head count, and Appendix B CoT prompt are unchanged. No new hardware, runtime, implementation, or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged. Section 7 expands descriptions of the same prior studies while retaining the positioning of OCR heads relative to visual, localization, and retrieval heads.

P1.justification: Section 6 becomes a two-subsection case study, preserving character recognition as Section 6.1 and adding distribution analysis as Section 6.2. Related work and the conclusion are expanded, Section 4.1 gains explanatory text, and acknowledgments are updated.

P2.justification: V2 adds a six-panel layer/head heatmap as Figure 7 and adjusts the sizing, spacing, and placement of retained displays. The unchanged appendix character heatmaps are renumbered from Figure 7 to Figure 8.

improvement.justification: Section 6.2 and Figure 7 add useful, inspectable evidence about head organization while preserving the earlier experiments and appendix detail. This limited gain is tempered by the conclusion's overly categorical 'unaffected' claim: unchanged Table 3 reports, for example, Qwen2-VL-7B HotpotQA falling from 49.6 to 47.5 when 20 OCR heads are masked.
